note: Curated dark-sky destinations. Coordinates approximate (nearest well-known viewpoint); bortle = typical class from published reports. Sources: DarkSky International place list, park service pages.

sites.name: Joshua Tree NP · Cottonwood / Pinto Basin
sites.note: Closest true dark sky to Orange County; the south end is darker than the north entrance.

sites.name: Anza-Borrego Desert SP · Borrego Springs
sites.note: Font's Point and Culp Valley are favourite spots; the town keeps its lights shielded.

sites.name: Death Valley NP · Harmony Borax / Zabriskie
sites.note: One of the darkest places in the lower 48; go in winter, summer nights stay hot.

sites.name: Big Bear · Big Bear Solar Observatory area
sites.note: Mountain darkness two hours from LA; light domes from the Inland Empire to the west.

sites.name: Mount Pinos · Chula Vista parking
sites.note: Classic southern California star party site at 2,600 m.

sites.name: Mojave National Preserve · Kelso Dunes
sites.note: Very dark; long drives and no services.

sites.name: Amboy Crater
sites.note: Off Route 66; flat horizons.

sites.name: Cerro Noroeste / Sierra Nevada backcountry
sites.note: Eastern Sierra; Bishop area with excellent transparency.

sites.name: Great Basin NP
sites.note: Among the darkest skies in the USA.

sites.name: Natural Bridges NM
sites.note: Owachomo Bridge under the Milky Way is the iconic shot.

sites.name: Bryce Canyon NP
sites.note: Annual astronomy festival in June.

sites.name: Capitol Reef NP
sites.note: Very dark, quiet campgrounds.

sites.name: Grand Canyon NP · South Rim
sites.note: Star party every June.

sites.name: Flagstaff · Lowell Observatory
sites.note: City with strict lighting laws; darker skies 30 min out of town.

sites.name: Kitt Peak area · Tohono O'odham
sites.note: Visitor centre night programs.

sites.name: Big Bend NP
sites.note: Least light-polluted national park in the lower 48.

sites.name: Enchanted Rock
sites.note: Close to Austin and San Antonio.

sites.name: Cherry Springs SP
sites.note: Best dark sky in the eastern USA; dedicated astronomy field.

sites.name: Headlands · Mackinaw City
sites.note: Aurora possible on the Lake Michigan shore.

sites.name: Cosmic Campground
sites.note: Gila National Forest; no lights for 60 km.

sites.name: Chaco Culture NHP
sites.note: Ancestral Puebloan astronomy site.

sites.name: Westcliffe & Silver Cliff
sites.note: Smokey Jack Observatory.

sites.name: Central Idaho Dark Sky Reserve · Stanley
sites.note: First reserve in the USA.

sites.name: Haleakalā summit
sites.note: Above the clouds at 3,055 m.

sites.name: Mauna Kea Visitor Station
sites.note: Stargazing at 2,800 m.

sites.name: Denali NP · Savage River
sites.note: Aurora season September–March.

sites.name: Everglades NP · Flamingo
sites.note: Darkest sky near Miami; mosquitoes in summer.

sites.name: Kissimmee Prairie Preserve SP
sites.note: Astronomy campsites bookable.

sites.name: Adirondacks · Tupper Lake
sites.note: Wild Center observatory events.

sites.name: Sundarbans · Kotka / Katka beach
sites.note: Darkest skies in Bangladesh; boat trips from Khulna/Mongla, permits required.

sites.name: Nijhum Dwip
sites.note: Remote island in the Meghna estuary; very few lights.

sites.name: Saint Martin's Island
sites.note: Dark sea horizons to the west; generator lights in the village.

sites.name: Sajek Valley
sites.note: Hill horizons, clouds below you in the monsoon; drier Nov–Feb.

sites.name: Tanguar Haor
sites.note: Houseboat nights on the haor; open horizons.

sites.name: Inani / Himchari beach
sites.note: South of Cox's Bazar town, away from the hotel lights.

sites.name: Kuakata beach
sites.note: Sea horizons to the south; town lights behind you.

sites.name: Lawachara forest · Srimangal
sites.note: Tea-garden country; Sylhet glow to the north.
